title: Decoration preserves obliviousness
statement: Let $P$ be a finite Turing machine over an alphabet $A$, let $l$ be a natural number, choose a work-tape index $h$ of $P$, a finite data-state set $D$ with initial state $d_0$, and any visit function of the specified type. Suppose every transition of $P$ emits no output symbol, and suppose that for any two inputs of equal length and every time, the input-head positions and all work-tape head positions of $P$ agree. Then the decorated machine has this same property: for any two inputs of equal length and every time, its input-head positions and all its work-tape head positions agree.
hypotheses_covered: $D$ is finite and has decidable equality
$P$ is a finite Turing machine over $A$
The visit function has the stated type
Every transition of $P$ emits no output symbol
$P$ is oblivious: equal-length inputs give equal input-head and work-tape head positions at every time
replaced:
Let $P$ be a machine over an alphabet $A$ whose transition table never emits an
output symbol, and suppose $P$ is oblivious. Then for every choice of data
transducer — number of extra tapes, designated head, finite data-state set with
initial element, and visit function — the decorated machine is oblivious. The data
states, emitted answers, and data-selected writes may depend arbitrarily on the
actual input; none of them can choose a head movement or terminate the schedule
early.
